request: I need an adapter to connect a hose with a 16 mm inner diameter to a pipe that is 25 mm OD. On the hose side there is a barbed nozzle: a 16 mm body carrying three ribs, each 0.8 mm high. On the pipe side there is a socket for the 25 mm pipe, its bore 0.15 mm bigger than the pipe (so 0.15 mm loose) and 20 mm deep, finishing in a shoulder the pipe butts against. The wall is 2 mm all the way along. A bore runs right through for the flow, the whole piece is 60 mm long, and going from one size to the other the profile mustn't be steeper than 45 degrees. I print it standing up (axis vertical) on an FDM printer in PLA without supports. Requirements: The hose side has a nozzle with a 16.0 mm body and exactly three barb ribs of 0.8 mm height each. The retention flank runs 30 to 45 degrees and the lead-in flank 10 to 30 degrees from the axis, so no retention flank is steeper than 45 degrees. Crests are 5.0 mm or more apart, the first at least 3.0 mm back from the tip and the last at least 4.0 mm before where the straight part ends; a 16 mm hose then pushes on and stays on. The nozzle's straight section must run at least 25 mm and the profile has to grow wider after it, so a pushed-on hose has something to grip and something to stop against. The straight section finishes 25.0 to 33.0 mm from the tip, and within 5.0 mm beyond that the outer radius reaches 11.0 mm (half of a 22 mm hose outside diameter). The pipe side is a 20.0 mm deep socket whose bore, 25.15 mm, is 0.15 mm larger than the 25 mm pipe, and it ends in a flat shoulder that stops the pipe, letting the pipe slide in and seat. The bore stays the same over its whole depth with no step or rib. The shoulder is square to the axis within 1.0 degree, at least 3.0 mm wide in the radial direction and backed by 2.0 mm or more of solid, and the 25 mm pipe seats with its end face within 0.10 mm of the shoulder. Both the spigot wall and the socket wall measure 2.0 to 2.4 mm, and nowhere is any wall thinner than 2.0 mm. Total length is 60.0 mm, with a bore through its entire length. Every section shares one axis, each within 0.10 mm of it, and the bore never narrows below 11.2 mm. On the outside, the shape changes from the 16 mm spigot to the socket in a single smooth transition: never steeper than 45 degrees from the axis, between 15 and 45 degrees from the axis, never narrowing, and with no step apart from the barb ribs. It finishes at the socket's outside diameter. It prints standing upright, axis vertical, with the spigot end on the bed. No overhang may be steeper than 45 degrees from vertical; the bed contact is 80 mm2 or more, the height is no more than four times the diameter of the bed face, and nothing is thinner than 0.8 mm. The whole adapter is a single manifold body. Apart from the two ends of the bore there must be no openings, and no internal cavity. Give me an STL, the OpenSCAD source, the declared layout and the agent's own measurement report, with that report agreeing to within 0.10 mm of an independent measurement.
